transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-08-18 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Samantha Ortiz (Pacific Health CTO), Ethan Park (Head of ML), Lina Gomez (IT Security)

[00:00:02] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Red wood Inference, with Maya on the SE side. we are gonna run through the model catalog demo and show how you pick open models and how the benchmarks are surfaced.
[00:00:12] Samantha: Great thanks. we have about 45 minutes, we wanna cover compatibility with our on-prem GPU fleet and some security questions.
[00:00:20] Maya: Perfect, we'll start with a quick product tour — console, API, and Optimize recommendations — then jump to the model catalog and benchmarks.
[00:00:30] Ethan: Quick qualifier: our main constraints are p95 latency < 200ms for 512 tokens and strict data residency, probably self-hosted or VPC.
[00:00:38] Jordan: Helpful. we'll point out dedicated and private options. just so you know, a lot of folks pick a hosted API for dev then move to dedicated.
[00:00:45] Lina: From security side, SOC2 is must, SSO/SAML, and we need KMS integration - HSM ideally.
[00:00:52] Maya: Absolutely, Redwood supports SSO, KMS, and for private we can do customer-managed keys. we also have audit logs and retention controls.
[00:01:05] Jordan: Alright jumping into the Console — here's the model catalog page, you can filter by license (open, commercial), by task, and by hardware compatibility.
[00:01:18] Maya: Note: the catalog shows benchmark tiles — throughput, latency p50/p95, and cost per 1k tokens. these are Redwood-verified using our benchmark harness. sometimes the vendor name in the transcript gets a bit off, e.g. Anthro-pic shows as anthro pick.
[00:01:35] Ethan: How often are these benchmarks updated?
[00:01:38] Maya: We run scheduled benchmarks nightly for the curated set and after any model or kernel change. for community models we run weekly; you also can run private bench tests in your Dedicated environment.
[00:01:52] Samantha: Show me an example of open models — we prefer permissive licenses.
[00:01:56] Maya: Sure, filter -> license: MIT/Apache. here we have Llama-2 variants, Mistral-7B, and a couple of LLMs like Red-wood-tuned- opens (note: transcript may show 'red wood tuned'). each has a compatibility matrix — supported quantization modes (INT8, FP16), supported hardware (A100, H100, L4), and max KV cache size.
[00:02:20] Jordan: The compatibility matrix is important — it lists which kernels are used per hardware, recommended sequence lengths, and whether the model supports continuous KV caching.
[00:02:30] Ethan: Our infra is a mix of A100 40GB and some L4s. will everything run?
[00:02:35] Maya: Most open models will run on A100 and L4; some INT8 kernels are H100-optimized. the matrix shows fallbacks — if a kernel isn't available we route to a compatible variant or use a different quant.
[00:02:47] Samantha: What about quantization effects on accuracy? we can't degrade clinical triage quality.
[00:02:52] Maya: Good question. Optimize provides per-model recommendations: it shows expected throughput uplift and measured quality delta on held-out evals. for some models INT8 gives ~2-3% metric drop, but often negligible for conversational tasks. we can attach your eval set to see exact deltas.
[00:03:08] Ethan: Is there an API to pull the compatibility matrix? we want to automate deployments.
[00:03:12] Jordan: Yes, the catalog API returns model metadata including supported hardware, quantization, and recommended compiler flags. example endpoint: GET /v1/models/catalog?filter=license:apache
[00:03:25] Samantha: Is that part of the hosted API or private plane?
[00:03:28] Maya: Both — the same catalog schema is available in hosted and private. for private, the control plane is customer-managed if you choose VPC/private.
[00:03:37] Lina: On encryption — KMS integration is supported in Private?
[00:03:40] Jordan: Yes, customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for private deployments. hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default but we can support BYOK for enterprise.
[00:03:50] [00:03:52] Speaker 1 (brief crosstalk): mm-hmm, yeah
[00:03:55] Maya: Back to benchmarks — here's a benchmark detail for Mistral-7B-quantized: p50 token latency 18ms, p95 82ms on L4 with INT8, cost per 1k tokens $0.22. notes: our transcriber sometimes writes L four as 'el four' and that creeps in.
[00:04:12] Ethan: Nice, can you show a comparison row for Llama-2-7B and Mistral?
[00:04:15] Maya: Sure, side-by-side: Llama-2-7b fp16 on A100 p95 120ms cost $0.35, Llama-2-7b int8 on L4 p95 95ms cost $0.18, Mistral-7b int8 on L4 p95 82ms cost $0.22. these numbers are from our 512-token gen profile.
[00:04:38] Samantha: We need to tune to our prompts; does Redwood support custom evals?
[00:04:42] Jordan: Yes, you can upload prompt sets and Redwood Optimize runs automated evals across models and quantization options, producing a quality vs cost chart.
[00:04:51] Ethan: Can the Optimize recommendations suggest batching and caching config?
[00:04:54] Maya: Exactly — Optimize suggests batching parameters, cache TTLs, and when prefix caching will help. it also recommends model variants for cost targets.
[00:05:05] Lina: From compliance: retention and logs — do you retain request payloads in hosted?
[00:05:09] Jordan: By default hosted retention is 30 days for debugging; enterprise can configure zero-retention or custom retention and export logs to your SIEM via S3 or syslog.
[00:05:19] Samantha: Good. show me the API flow for swapping models in a route — we might want automatic fallback if default model is saturated.
[00:05:27] Maya: In the Console you create a route, pin a model version, set rollout policy — canary, A/B, fallback tiers. API: POST /v1/routes with policy object, e.g. route.primary=model-a, route.fallbacks=[model-b, model-c].
[00:05:44] Ethan: How do you measure regressions? we have a small test mean set.
[00:05:47] Maya: Redwood ties evals to rollouts; before promoting a model you run regression tests on your eval set; if quality drops beyond threshold, the rollout fails and it falls back.
[00:05:58] [00:06:00] Jordan: Quick pause for questions.
[00:06:04] Samantha: What about throughput guarantees on Dedicated? our production needs 200qps sustained, spikes to 800.
[00:06:11] Maya: Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools. we size pools by expected tokens/sec; autoscaling policies can add burst capacity. we also provide SLAs for uptime and latency for enterprise contracts.
[00:06:24] Ethan: Any benchmarks for long context — 8k or 32k?
[00:06:28] Maya: The catalog tags models with supported context lengths and kernel-level optimizations for long context. we publish benchmarks for 2k/8k/32k profiles. note: longer contexts increase KV cache memory — the compatibility matrix shows max sequence support per GPU.
[00:06:43] Samantha: If we run private on-prem, will we still get the same Optimize recommendations?
[00:06:47] Jordan: Yes, Optimize can run on your private control plane; you can supply local benchmark data and Optimize will suggest configurations tailored to your hardware.
[00:06:58] Lina: A security nit — do you store model weights or are they pulled from customer repos?
[00:07:03] Maya: For private/on-prem we don't store weights outside your network. for hosted we cache weights in encrypted storage but can support BYO weights for special contracts.
[00:07:14] Ethan: About model licensing: some open models have restrictions — can you surface license risk?
[00:07:18] Maya: The catalog displays license type and a risk flag if the model's license is ambiguous. we also provide suggested alternatives with clearer terms.
[00:07:28] Samantha: We also want a compatibility matrix export for our orchestration team.
[00:07:32] Jordan: Sure — you can export CSV/JSON. Maya will share a link after the call.
[00:07:37] [00:07:40] Speaker 2 (murmur): okay great
[00:07:43] Maya: Switching to API demo: here's a sample call for generating with model id, and how to request streaming tokens. note: streaming is supported across hosted/dedicated but on private you may need a websocket proxy depending on network.
[00:07:58] Ethan: Can we get per-token cost breakdown on traces?
[00:08:02] Jordan: Yes the Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route. that helps spot expensive prompts.
[00:08:10] Samantha: Clarify fallback behavior again — is there a route weight or strict fallback?
[00:08:14] Maya: Both. you can set weights for A/B, or define strict fallbacks where primary -> fallback only on error or capacity.
[00:08:24] Ethan: For pilot we'd like a small trial with 50k tokens/day on Dedicated. can we get a quote?
[00:08:29] Jordan: Yes, I'll send pricing. typical pilot includes reserved nodes for the trial period.
[00:08:33] Samantha: Timeline: if the pilot is okay, we aim to be live in Q4.
[00:08:38] Jordan: Sounds feasible.
[00:08:40] Maya: One more advanced note — kernel selection: our runtime chooses kernels based on seq length distribution, hardware, and whether KV caching is on. that influences latency and memory.
[00:08:52] Ethan: Does the catalog show which kernels are used?
[00:08:55] Maya: Yes, the compatibility matrix includes kernel hints and a recommended compiler flag set.
[00:09:02] Samantha: Any regulatory stuff for healthcare? do you support HIPAA-required controls?
[00:09:06] Lina: we'll need HIPAA BAA for any PHI handling.
[00:09:09] Jordan: Redwood has enterprise compliance options; HIPAA is supported on Private with contractual BAAs and dedicated hosting. we'll share the compliance pack.
[00:09:18] [00:09:20] Maya: Demo end-to-end: pick model -> run eval -> view Optimize suggestion -> promote to route with canary.
[00:09:29] Samantha: Good demo. can you show the benchmark CSV now?
[00:09:33] Maya: sharing link in chat: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/pacific-demo (note: link may be placeholder in transcript). the CSV includes p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU mem, quant mode, kernel notes.
[00:09:47] Ethan: We'll run our eval set against those numbers.
[00:09:50] Jordan: Recap/next steps: I'll send pricing and SOW; Maya will share benchmark sheet, compatibility matrix export, and a proposal for a 2-week Dedicated pilot. Pacific to provide sample prompts and security questionnaire.
[00:10:05] Samantha: Thanks, this was helpful.
[00:10:08] Lina: Thanks. we'll review and get the questionnaire back.
[00:10:12] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up this week.
[00:10:15] End of recording — rest of the 45m was Q&A and scheduling logistics; transcript truncated for brevity.
